entries.subject: A false color from three measured bands, as the HR 8799 planets have
entries.finding: Shown in infrared false color from its measured flux in 2MASS Ks 2.159 µm, 2MASS H 1.662 µm, 2MASS J 1.235 µm (Bohn et al. (2020a), as compiled in Best, Liu, Magnier & Dupuy (2024), The UltracoolSheet v2.1 (Zenodo); zero points from the SVO Filter Profile Service). Hoch et al. (2025) publish JWST spectra of this planet, but no paper gives its flux densities in the NIRCam F410M, F430M and F460M bands that color HR 8799's planets. Band fluxes computed here from the spectrum would be a derived value, not a published one.
entries.revisitWhen: Flux densities in three bands comparable with HR 8799's are published.

entries.subject: The dusty disc around YSES 1 b
entries.finding: Hoch et al. (2025) detect silicate emission from submicron olivine grains in a disc around the planet. No paper gives the disc's size or orientation, so it is not drawn.
entries.revisitWhen: The disc is resolved or its extent is modelled in a paper.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret, Hauschildt & Witte (2012), A&A 546, A14 compute from PHOENIX model atmospheres for the H band at 1,727 K and log g 3.59 (u1 0.791, u2 -0.029): a model, not a measurement of this planet. Its temperature is the 1,727 K of its measurements record; log g 3.59 follows from the mass and radius of its astronomy record (packages/astronomy/data/bodies/yses-1-b.json).
